label: Harm and care action verbs
explanation: Fires on verbs describing consequential actions directed at another being, with killing as the prototype — " kill" fires on 81% of its occurrences and the strongest activations are kills/killing/slew/assassinate/duels in narrative and plot-summary contexts, with spillover onto adjacent prepositions, possessives, and articles that introduce the target ("duels with Edmund", "kills his step-dad", "war against the Pope"). The pattern extends moderately to care/affection verbs (love 13%, "care for", help, hold, like kissing) and other harm verbs (hit, injuring, destroy, eat in food-chain contexts). It stays silent in neutral text; the frequent prepositions " with"/" for"/" of"/" to" fire at only ~1% conditional rate, i.e. as spillover inside activating verb phrases rather than as independent triggers.
